Smt. Kalibai vs Ishwar on 5 February, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Ind:3809

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Binod Kumar Dwivedi
 On The 5 th Of February, 2026
 Misc. Appeal No. 719 of 2017
 Smt. Kalibai And Others
 Versus
 Ishwar And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Ankit Gandhi - Advocate appearing on behalf of Shri 
 Advocate for appellants.

Order 
This appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 23/01/2017 passed by Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jhabua (M.P.) in Claim Case No.127/2014, whereby claim petition filed on behalf of the claimants /
survivors of the deceased Mangla, has been dismissed.

2. Brief facts of the case are that on 29/06/2014 the deceased aged about 35 years had gone for fixing the marriage of his brother Joga's daughter on motorcycle to Village Maachliyajhar, when he reached on the spot, respondent No.1 Ishwar came there on motorcycle bearing registration number MP-45-MC- 1708 driven rashly and negligently dashed the motorcycle of Mangla, wherein he has suffered grievous injuries and passed away on the next date i.e. on 30/06/2014 during treatment.
FIR was lodged on the same day by the wife of the deceased Kaalibai and criminal case was registered.
After that survivors of the deceased filed claim petition claiming compensation to the tune of Rs.17,25,000/- for untimely death of Mangla in a road traffic accident.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3809 2 MA-719-2017 3.
Learned counsel for the appellants / claimants submits that claim petition has been dismissed only on conjectures and surmises instead of deciding it on merits and evidence available on record.

He further submits that on the same day i.e. 29/06/2014 FIR (Ex.-P/1) was lodged by wife of the deceased Kaalibai against the driver of the offending vehicle bearing registration number MP-45-MC-1708 and after investigation charge sheet (Ex.-P/5) was filed.
He further submits that MLC report along with postmortem report has also been filed on the record.
There was no occasion to dismiss the claim petition.
For this he has invited attention of this Court towards para 10 of the impugned award.

On these submissions, learned counsel prays for allowing this appeal by setting Smt. Kalibai vs Ishwar on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74965206/

aside the impugned award and to appropriate amount of compensation.
4. None appeared on behalf of the respondents, even after service of notice.

5. Heard and considered the submissions raised at bar and perused the record.
6.

The case of the appellants is that on the date of accident, Nabu (AW-2) along with his brother Mangla has gone on separate motorcycles to village for fixing the marriage of elder brother's Joga's daughter.
When they were returning, deceased Mangla was on the separate motorcycle.

Ahead of him when they reached on the spot respondent No.1 Ishwar on his motorcycle bearing registration number MP-45-MC-1708 came driving rashly and negligently and collided with the motorcycle of deceased, which resulted in injuries and after that respondent No.1 Ishwar fled away.
Mangla was taken to the Hospital and during treatment on the next day he passed away.

7. The same has been corroborated by the Kaalibai (AW-1), therefore, the evidence on this count is intact and nothing adverse has surfaced in the testimony NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:3809 3 MA-719-2017 of the aforesaid witnesses.

Statement of the aforesaid witnesses are corroborated by FIR (Ex.-P/1), MLC Report (Ex.-P/2), Postmortem Report (Ex.-P/3)
and Charge Sheet (Ex.-P/5).
Thus, it is well proved that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the aforesaid motorcycle by respondent No.1 Ishwar.
8. Kaalibai (AW-1) stated in her statement stated that her husband deceased Mangla was near about 35 years of age.
No other evidence like Birth Certificate has been filed.
There is a difference of age in the MLC Report (Ex.-P/2), wherein it is mentioned as 42 years and in the postmortem report (Ex.-P/3) it is 35 years.
Thus, the age of the deceased could be taken in between 41 to 45 years.

9. Since no relevant proof with regard to income of the deceased is there, his income can be assessed at Rs.5,845/- considering him as skilled labour in light of the circular issued by Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh under the Minimum Wages Act, therefore, income of the deceased is assessed at Rs.5,845/- per month as skilled labour.

sentences.text:
11. In the light of para 59.4 of the judgment by the Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (Supra) ,
considering the age of deceased between 41 to 45 years, 25% amount is added in the head of Future Prospects.
12.

Similarly, as per para 59.8 of the Pranay Sethi's judgment (Supra), an amount of Rs.40,000/-
each is added in the head of Loss of Consortium.
Since claimants are five in numbers, therefore, the amount of Loss of Consortium comes to Rs.2,00,000/-.

In the head of Loss of Estate and Funeral Expenses Rs.15,000/-

2 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3809 4 MA-719-2017 each is added.
13.

Thus, the just and proper compensation comes as under:
Rs.5,845.00 per month + Rs.1461.25 (25% F.P.) = Rs.7,306.25 x 12 = Rs.87,675.00 - Rs.21,918.75
Loss of Dependency: (1/4th Personal Expenses) = Rs.65,756.25 x 14 (Multiplier) = Rs.9,20,587.50 (round off to Rs.9,20,600/-) Consortium Rs.2,00,000.00

Loss of estate Rs.15,000.00 Funeral Rs.15,000.00 expenses Total:
Rs.11,50,600.00
Thus, the amount is enhanced and appellants / claimants are entitled for an amount of Rs.11,50,600/-.
The amount of compensation will carry simple interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition.
14. Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellants / claimants is allowed to the extent as indicated hereinabove.
